title: How does a fridge keep things cold?
examples: Does the fridge use electricity to make cold?
What happens to the heat that leaves the fridge?
Is the cooling process related to water evaporating?

explain.say: Say, heat always moves from warm places to cool places.

draw.text: How does a fridge keep things cold?

explain.say: Say, when liquids turn into gas, they take heat energy from their surroundings.
say, this process is called evaporation, and it cools things down.
say, the fridge uses a special liquid called refrigerant to cycle heat.
say, the refrigerant evaporates inside the fridge, taking heat out of the food.
say, in real life, opening a cold drink can makes it feel warmer quickly.

faq.q: Does the fridge actually create coldness?
faq.a: No, the fridge does not create coldness; it moves existing heat outside the box. It simply transfers heat from the inside to the outside environment.

faq.q: Where does the heat that is taken out go?
faq.a: The heat is transferred out of the fridge through the condenser coils, usually at the back or bottom. This heat is then released into the room air.

faq.q: Is the refrigerant gas or liquid?
faq.a: The refrigerant changes between liquid and gas states during the cycle. This phase change is what allows it to absorb and release heat effectively.
asks: Does it need to be both?
What state does it need to be?

faq.a: Yes, the compressor needs electrical energy to push the refrigerant gas through the system. The electricity powers the movement, not the cooling itself.
Yes, when a liquid evaporates, it takes energy (heat) from its surroundings to change state. This removal of heat causes the surrounding area to cool down.
asks: Is cooling always linked to gas?

facts: Heat naturally moves from warmer objects to cooler objects.
Evaporation is the process where a liquid turns into a gas.
Phase changes, like liquid to gas, require or release energy.
Refrigerators move heat from inside to outside.

quiz.say: If you leave a puddle of water on a hot day, what happens to the water?

options.show: The water turns into steam instantly.
options.say: The water turns into steam instantly.

options.show: The water just disappears without changing.
options.say: The water just disappears without changing.

options.show: The heat energy is trapped inside the puddle.
options.say: The heat energy is trapped inside the puddle.

options.show: It evaporates, taking heat energy from the surroundings.
options.say: It evaporates, taking heat energy from the surroundings.

quiz.why: Evaporation is a cooling process because the liquid needs energy to become a gas.

wrong.0: Steam is boiling, which requires much more heat than simple evaporation.
wrong.1: Matter must change state to leave as a gas.
wrong.2: Heat always moves from hot areas to cooler areas.

quiz.say: In a refrigeration cycle, what part is responsible for releasing the heat outside?
quiz.show: Heat is released at the condenser.

options.show: The expansion valve releases the heat.
options.say: The expansion valve releases the heat.

options.show: The condenser releases the heat energy outside the fridge.
options.say: The condenser releases the heat energy outside the fridge.

options.show: The compressor absorbs all the heat.
options.say: The compressor absorbs all the heat.

quiz.why: The condenser is where the high-pressure gas cools down and releases the collected heat.

wrong.0: The expansion valve controls pressure, it does not release the main heat load.
wrong.2: The evaporator is inside and is where the cooling happens.
wrong.3: The compressor only moves the gas; it does not store the heat.

quiz.say: If the refrigerant is in the gas state inside the fridge, what is happening?

options.show: It is being compressed by the motor.
options.say: It is being compressed by the motor.

options.show: It is absorbing heat from the food inside the fridge.
options.say: It is absorbing heat from the food inside the fridge.

options.show: It is releasing heat into the food.
options.say: It is releasing heat into the food.

options.show: It is staying at a constant temperature.
options.say: It is staying at a constant temperature.

quiz.why: The gas absorbing heat is the key step that removes warmth from the contents.

wrong.0: Compression happens, but the primary action for cooling is heat absorption.
wrong.2: Releasing heat would make the food warmer, which is the opposite of cooling.
wrong.3: The process relies on a temperature change to move heat.
